executiveSummary: Surveillance signals from ECDC and PAHO covering late 2025 through May 2026 indicate multiple concurrent biological threats across the Americas and Europe. The most pressing concerns include ongoing Avian Influenza A(H5N1) activity in the Americas with persistent zoonotic spillover risk, a dengue epidemic of significant scale, and the start of the Southern Hemisphere influenza season coinciding with RSV co-circulation. Additional elevated threats include mpox transmission in the Americas, a measles resurgence, pertussis surges, yellow fever activity, and chikungunya spread, reflecting strain on regional immunization and surveillance systems.
bottomLine: The Americas face an unusually high concurrent burden of vector-borne, vaccine-preventable, and zoonotic diseases in 2025-2026, with Avian Influenza A(H5N1) and dengue representing the highest-priority threats requiring immediate coordinated response.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Multiple PAHO epidemiological updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating ongoing spread
Zoonotic spillover risk to humans from animal reservoir; ECDC concurrent monitoring in Europe
threats.action: Enhance surveillance at human-animal interface, enforce biosafety at poultry and dairy farms, stockpile antiviral countermeasures, and prepare pandemic response protocols

threats.name: Dengue
signals: Epidemiological update issued February 2026 indicating elevated regional transmission
Historically high case counts consistent with hyperendemic multi-serotype circulation and expanding Aedes aegypti range
threats.action: Activate vector control programs, strengthen case management capacity, issue traveler advisories, and accelerate dengue vaccine deployment in eligible populations

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued April 2026 confirming ongoing transmission
Continued human-to-human spread across multiple countries in the region
threats.action: Scale up vaccination with MVA-BN vaccine, enhance contact tracing, strengthen laboratory diagnostic capacity, and issue guidance for at-risk communities

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza and RSV Co-circulation
signals: PAHO alert April 2026 marking start of Southern Hemisphere influenza season
PAHO January 2026 alert on simultaneous influenza and RSV circulation stressing healthcare systems
threats.action: Promote influenza vaccination before season peak, strengthen hospital surge capacity, prioritize RSV prophylaxis for high-risk infants and elderly

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two separate PAHO updates issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained elevated case counts
Resurgence suggests waning immunity and potential vaccination coverage gaps
threats.action: Audit and strengthen vaccination coverage including booster programs for adolescents and adults, implement cocooning strategy for neonates, and enhance laboratory-confirmed surveillance

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued March 2026 indicating active transmission
Epizootics in non-human primates serving as early warning signal for human spillover risk
threats.action: Ensure vaccination coverage in endemic zones, enforce International Health Regulations vaccination requirements for travelers, and strengthen primate mortality surveillance

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 indicating resurgence
Transmission in populations with vaccination coverage gaps post-COVID-19 disruptions
threats.action: Conduct catch-up mass vaccination campaigns targeting under-vaccinated communities, strengthen case-based surveillance, and enforce mandatory reporting of suspected cases

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 indicating active circulation
Co-circulation with dengue in Aedes-endemic zones complicates clinical differentiation and burden estimation
threats.action: Enhance integrated arboviral surveillance, strengthen vector control, and ensure clinical guidance for differential diagnosis from dengue and Zika

amrSignals: No explicit AMR-specific reports identified in this report set; however, Bordetella pertussis macrolide resistance warrants monitoring given sustained transmission despite vaccination
Potential for secondary bacterial infections in dengue and influenza cases driving empiric antibiotic use and selection pressure in high-burden settings
emergingPatterns: Concurrent multi-pathogen burden in the Americas in 2026 suggests systemic vulnerabilities in immunization infrastructure and vector control programs
Southern Hemisphere influenza season onset combined with RSV co-circulation signals potential healthcare surge risk for mid-2026
Back-to-back PAHO H5N1 updates in November 2025 and March 2026 suggest sustained and potentially expanding zoonotic interface activity
Resurgence of vaccine-preventable diseases (measles, pertussis) consistent with pandemic-era immunization disruptions not yet fully recovered
Co-circulation of multiple arboviruses (dengue, chikungunya) in the same Aedes-endemic zones increases diagnostic complexity and may mask true burden
